title: Chapter 11. The Lamp of Navadvipa
html:
Navadvipa is non-different from Vrindavana; Mayapura is Goloka itself; the cause of Gaura's descent — Krishna's three desires; bhajana in the eight periods of the day according to Gaura's lila; the acharya is one who knows the truth of Krishna, not one bound to varna (pp. 30–31)

[p. 30]

1In the universe blessed is the Earth; on Earth blessed is the land of Gauda;
in Gauda blessed is Navadvipa, sixteen kroshas, honoured by the world.

2In its midst blessed is the swift-flowing Bhagirathi,
with which Sri Yamuna and Sarasvati come and merge.1

3On its eastern bank is Mayapura, Goloka itself:
there, in Sri Shachi's house, shines Gauranga Thakura.

4That Thakura who at the end of the Dvapara age, in the forests of Vrindavana,
performed the great rasa with Radhika and the other gopis —

5the son of Nanda and Yashoda — brought together with Vraja
the great rasa of parakiya, the eternal treasure of Goloka.2

6That Thakura has again brought into the world, into Gauda,
His own "yoga-maya-pura", He who is expert in tasting rasa.3

7In Sri Krishna's lila three desires were not fulfilled;
in Sri Gaura's lila He fulfilled them, attaining that happiness:4

8"What happiness does Radha find in loving Me?
How much delight has Radha in tasting My sweetness?

[p. 31]

9What is Radha's bliss when She realizes Me?
Being the hero, I do not understand the essence of this happiness.

10Therefore, taking Radha's mood and lustre, I shall become Gaura
and, in the mood of a devotee, taste Krishna's sweetness and the rest."

11Thinking thus, Krishna with His abode came to Gauda:
in Navadvipa He Himself appeared, rapt in bliss.

12O brother, leave everything and live in Navadvipa:
serve Gauranga in the eight periods of the day, and sorrow will go.

13In the eight periods is the eightfold lila of Krishna, its essence:
serve in the mood revealed by Gaura, and you will gain wondrous prema.

14Whoever has a mind wholly set on serving Krishna,
let him, in the eight periods of Gauda, serve the treasure of Krishna's rasa.5

15Whoever wants to serve Krishna without knowing Gaura's mood —
to him the transcendent truth of Krishna will never be revealed.

16Whether one is within varna, within ashrama, or outside varna and ashrama —
whoever knows the truth of Krishna is the experienced acharya.6

17Whoever, leaving the essential, brother, honours varna,
accepting a false guru, ruins both past and future.

Notes

  1. Cf. the teaching of Navadvipa as the confluence of three rivers (Triveni) in Bhaktivinoda Thakura's Navadvipa-dhama-mahatmya.
  2. "Parakiya" — the love of the gopis for Krishna as a "paramour", the highest form of prema in Vraja. According to Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati this is wholly transcendent prema, having nothing in common with worldly passion or worldly adultery.
  3. A play on words: Mayapura is the "city of yogamaya", the Lord's internal energy, not of material maya.
  4. Krishna's three desires — cf. CC Adi 1.6 and Adi 4 (the verse of Svarupa Damodara); verses 8–10 render them in the poet's own words.
  5. Ashta-kala — the eight periods of the day. The reference appears to be to Gaura's "ashtakaliya-lila", remembrance of which leads to remembrance of the lila of Radha and Krishna.
  6. Cf. CC Madhya 8.127: whether brahmana, sannyasi or shudra — whoever knows the truth of Krishna is guru.
